IL-2025-HB1004.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Military Veterans Assistance Act, in the section that gives the law its short title. It affects that law’s wording only.

IL-2025-HB1049.s: The bill would require a court to order child support when someone is convicted of aggravated drunk driving that causes a death. It applies to the minor children of the victim or victims. It also sets a way to figure out the child support amount and makes a related change in the vehicle law.

IL-2025-HB106.s: This bill would appropriate $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Department of Juvenile Justice for its FY26 ordinary and contingent expenses. It would take effect on July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB110.s: This bill would appropriate $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Department of Public Health for its FY26 ordinary and contingent expenses. It would take effect on July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1158.s: This law changes how the Metropolitan Water Reclamation District can issue bonds, notes, and other debt for certain purposes. It raises the most that can be issued in one budget year to $250 million, up from $150 million, plus any unused amount from the prior three budget years. It takes effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB12.s: The bill would raise Illinois’s estate tax exclusion, which is the amount that can pass before the tax applies, from $4 million to $6 million. It would apply to people who die on or after January 1, 2026, and would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB124.s: This bill would appropriate $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Office of the Executive Inspector General for the Attorney General. The money would be for the office’s FY26 ordinary and contingent expenses, and the bill would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB128.s: The bill would give $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Office of the Executive Inspector General for the Treasurer for its FY26 regular and special expenses. It applies to that office only. The measure would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1310.s: The bill would change pension rules for Tier 2 downstate firefighters. It would stop cutting the pension for some firefighters who retire after age 50 with 20 or more years of service, and it would raise yearly pension increases to start at age 55 instead of 60 and set them at 3% of the original pension. These changes would apply right away and would be carried out without state reimbursement.

IL-2025-HB1330.s: The bill would raise pay rates for in-home services under Illinois’s Community Care Program, starting January 1, 2026, if federal approval is given. It ties the higher rate to a $20-an-hour minimum wage for direct service workers and requires providers to certify they are following the wage rule and to file cost reports. It also says fringe benefits cannot be cut because of the higher rates, and starting January 1, 2028, providers must spend at least 80% of program payments on pay and other compensation for these workers.

IL-2025-HB1366.s: Creates a notice rule for schools that work with children with disabilities. Schools would have to tell parents or guardians in writing that they can bring an IEP advocate to meetings about a child’s education plan and can ask for an IEP facilitator, which is a person who helps guide the meeting. The notice could be given with other school papers, such as enrollment forms. The law takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB1375.s: The bill would create a student teaching stipend program and set rules for how stipend money is given out. It would also let student teachers count that service toward optional pension credit, and it would change how certain teacher pay increases are handled so stipends for cooperating teachers are not counted in that part of the pension law. Educator preparation programs would have to report eligible students and cooperating teachers, and eligible cooperating teachers who get a stipend would need to finish specific training. The measure would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB138.s: This measure would appropriate $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Illinois Community College Board. The money would be for the board’s FY26 ordinary and contingent expenses, and it would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1433.s: Colleges and universities could choose to give academic credit, or another non-credit option, to students who serve as election judges. If a judge gets that school credit, they could not also get other pay or compensation under the Election Code.

IL-2025-HB1446.s: The bill would require police agencies to set up temporary firearm storage programs, and it would also allow some licensed and state-certified private businesses to do so. A gun owner would have to fill out a request form, choose how long the gun will be held, and agree that it will be turned over if not picked up on time. Police would have to give notice before storage ends, post program details online if they have a public website, and use a warrant to use a stored gun for any purpose. The law would take effect one year after it becomes law.

IL-2025-HB149.s: This bill would appropriate $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Illinois Medical District Commission. The money would be for the commission’s ordinary and contingent expenses for FY26. It would take effect on July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1505.s: Changes several racing rules in Illinois. It lets the Racing Board name a person to handle some wagering duties, sends certain pari-mutuel tax money to the Board, and changes how grant money is handed out to a charity. It also ends some old rules about daily fee deposits and horse drug testing at county fairs. It became law on August 15, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1552.s: The bill would create a new state law for school district impact notes. It would require the Illinois State Board of Education to write a short note on certain bills that could hurt a school district's finances or add staffing work, and the note would describe the bill's expected effect on education. It also says the bill material sent to the board must be kept private before a bill is introduced. The law would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-HB156.s: The bill would give $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Illinois Workers' Compensation Commission for its FY26 everyday and needed extra costs. It would take effect on July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1598.s: The bill would set training, certification, or work experience rules for surgical technologists hired or contracted by a health care facility on or after January 1, 2027. It would affect health care facilities and the people they hire for surgical technology work. It also says people may still do this work if they are working within their own license or registration, or if they are students or interns under direct supervision.

IL-2025-HB1616.s: Illinois law now lets part-time employees and other covered workers use up to 10 days of leave in a 12-month period to serve as an organ donor. For part-time workers, employers must pay them based on their average daily pay from the previous 2 months while they use this leave. The law takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB163.s: This bill would appropriate $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Office of the Legislative Inspector General. The money would be for the office’s FY26 ordinary and contingent expenses. It would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1763.s: The bill would stop social clubs from charging a member for time when the member is not allowed in the club or cannot use its services because the member is delinquent or in poor standing. It would make any contract that breaks this rule void and unenforceable, and a violation would count as an unfair business practice under Illinois consumer fraud law. The rule would not apply to contracts signed before the law takes effect, and it would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-HB1774.s: The bill would move $100,000 from the Build Illinois Bond Fund to the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity. The money would be used for a grant to the City of Calumet City to help pay for infrastructure improvements. It would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1787.s: The law requires school districts to train substitute staff on school evacuation drills and law enforcement lockdown drills. It affects school personnel who work in substitute roles. It became law as Public Act 104-0198 and takes effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB180.s: The bill would give $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Office of the State Appellate Defender for its FY26 regular and extra-needed expenses. It would take effect on July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB1863.s: Creates a task force in the Illinois Department of Public Health to make a plan for better teamwork among doctors, veterinarians, other science experts, and state agencies. The group would work on ways to support the health of people, animals, and the environment, and would include set members who meet at the chairperson’s call. Members would not be paid, but could be repaid for needed expenses, and the task force would send a final report to state leaders by January 1, 2027.

IL-2025-HB1864.s: This law changes rules for electronic billing between dental care providers and dental plan carriers in Illinois. It lets some providers claim an exemption, and those providers must file a form with the Department of Insurance. It also requires carriers to offer portals for benefit and billing info, electronic claim filing, electronic attachments, and payment details, and to allow other payment methods without extra fees if a provider asks.

IL-2025-HB1927.s: The bill would stop money in the Open Space Lands Acquisition and Development Fund from being moved, assigned, or sent to another state fund. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB198.s: Creates the Fiscal Year 2026 Budget Implementation Act, a law to carry out the state budget, and would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB208.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Business Corporation Act of 1983. It affects the part of the law that gives the act its short name.

IL-2025-HB212.s: Would make a small technical change to the Illinois Benefit Corporation Act in the section that gives the law its short name.

IL-2025-HB230.s: The bill would make a technical change to a section of the Payday Loan Reform Act that covers the short title. It would affect the state rules for payday loans.

IL-2025-HB2327.s: The law makes a technical change to the Labor Dispute Act’s short-title section. It became Public Act 104-0016 and takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB2346.s: Makes the Illinois Department of Public Health share on its website which pharmacies take part in the drug reuse program, teach pharmacies how to join, and publish public materials about the program. It also requires the department to collect participant information and send a yearly report to lawmakers starting December 31, 2026. The law takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB2397.s: This law may be called the Eddie Thomas Act and amends Illinois prison rules. It requires the Department of Corrections to post a yearly website report on hospice and palliative care in its prisons and other facilities, including who used the care, how many people were in the programs, when care was given, how many people died, staff levels, policies, and program costs. The data must be kept anonymous, and the law takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB2418.s: The law creates a Youth Sports Commission in Illinois to study youth sports and make recommendations on access, safety, growth, and youth development. The Department of Human Services will help support the commission. The commission must send a report by December 31, 2025, and every year after that. It became law on August 15, 2025.

IL-2025-HB2436.s: The law changes when a public defender in a county over 3 million people can handle immigration cases. It limits that work to cases in the county or for county residents with cases outside the county, unless the county board allows more. It became law on August 15, 2025.

IL-2025-HB2442.s: Vehicles used by local emergency services and disaster agencies could install and use a traffic signal preemption device when they are answering a real emergency and using red flashing, rotating, or oscillating lights. A traffic signal preemption device can change traffic signals so emergency vehicles can pass through more easily. The law takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB2498.s: Requires the Department of Children and Family Services to send the Illinois General Assembly a yearly report by March 1. The report would cover the department’s open case files, its caseload tracking system, and the ratio of active cases to active staff. It would also look at how funding could be set up to encourage the department to manage caseloads and reduce the load on individual workers.

IL-2025-HB2547.s: The law updates state laws to use "Department of Veterans Affairs" instead of "Department of Veterans' Affairs". It applies to the Department of Veterans Affairs and took effect on August 15, 2025.

IL-2025-HB255.s: The bill would make a technical change to the short title section of the Illinois Code of Civil Procedure. It affects civil court law in Illinois, but the change is only a wording update.

IL-2025-HB2572.s: The law changes who decides if people can get certain veterans' dependent scholarships and grants in Illinois. It says the Department of Veterans' Affairs must set the rules for who is eligible, and it takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB2641.s: The bill would exempt certain home property from school district property taxes if it is owned by a person who will be 67 or older during that tax year. It applies to homestead property, which is a person's main home. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB2651.s: The bill would require the State Board of Education to post and share, by February 1 each year, a list of days in the next school year when many students may miss or not take part in a major school event because of cultural, religious, or other observances. School districts could add more days based on local feedback or student makeup, and the list would also be sent to other education groups and offices. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB2677.s: The bill would change Illinois estate tax rules for estates that include qualified farm property. It would set a $6,000,000 exemption for figuring the state death tax credit, instead of a $4,000,000 exclusion amount, and that amount would be adjusted each year for inflation using the Consumer Price Index. It would also change how a deceased spouse's unused exclusion amount is figured, and would change the special farm land value rules and the term "qualified heir."

IL-2025-HB2695.s: Creates a state study on pay and benefits for human services jobs funded by the Illinois Department of Human Services. The department would also set up a task force to review the study and make recommendations on worker pay, hiring, and retention, including a plan to raise rates by July 1, 2030. It also requires yearly reports on pay gaps and the money needed to reduce them, and it would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB2726.s: Now law in Illinois, this measure gives the Department of Natural Resources power to take steps for "rewilding" as a conservation plan. That includes restoring land to a more natural state, bringing back native species, and restoring natural ecological processes. It takes effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB2751.s: Illinois law now lets police or other local officers order a tow if a car is for sale and its vehicle ID number has been destroyed, removed, covered, altered, or defaced. It also bars dealers, or people acting like dealers, from parking a car mainly to sell it on public streets, public lots, other public property, or private property that the public may drive on. The law creates a task force to review unlicensed dealer enforcement, lets some licenses be denied, revoked, or suspended, and raises some fines from $50 to $1,000 to $3,000 per violation. It takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB2774.s: Creates a single phone number for people to get help and referrals for domestic violence services in Illinois. The Department of Human Services would run the system and could hire a lead group to manage and oversee a statewide hotline that is toll-free, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and offers help in many languages. The lead group must also help people who are deaf or hard of hearing and give regular reports to the department. It became Public Act 104-0247 and takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB287.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Non-Support Punishment Act. It affects a section that gives the law its short name.

IL-2025-HB2870.s: The bill would change Illinois film tax credits for accredited productions and split them into two types based on where filming happens and how much spending takes place at a qualified production site. It would also change the credit amount, the rules for counting some nonresident worker wages, and the meaning of a qualified production facility. It would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-HB2873.s: Changes Illinois stalking law to include certain harassment that would upset a reasonable person and that also causes emotional distress to the person asking for protection. It says some actions are presumed to cause distress, including repeated calls, following, surveillance, disturbing a workplace or school, and threats against a child, family member, or with physical force. The law took effect on August 15, 2025.

IL-2025-HB2887.s: The bill would change Illinois' public records law for people who make many requests. It would lower the number of requests needed to count someone as a recurrent requester, and public bodies would have 30 days instead of 21 to answer those requests. It would also require notice about recurrent requests only once every 30 days, and people in that group would have to say so when getting a public record.

IL-2025-HB2891.s: The bill would change rules for water commissions in Illinois. It would let them use design-build contracts, which are contracts that cover both design and building, and set goals for buying goods, services, and construction work. It would also let them build water lines up to 50 miles outside member cities and keep commissioner pay at no more than $10,000 a year.

IL-2025-HB305.s: Would make a small technical change to a state law section about grievances filed by people in custody.

IL-2025-HB3076.s: The bill would appropriate $7,500,000 from the General Revenue Fund to the Department of Human Services. It would give a grant to the Illinois Network of Centers for Independent Living to administer and implement the Home Modification Program.

IL-2025-HB3081.s: The bill would create an Out-of-School Time Advisory Council to advise the governor and state agencies on after-school and other out-of-school programs. It would give guidance on funding, service quality, access for children who need these programs most, and annual reporting. The changes would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB3087.s: The law changes rules for methamphetamine precursor products, which are medicines with ingredients like ephedrine or pseudoephedrine. It raises the amount allowed in each targeted package to 3,600 milligrams and removes a rule that limited a single person to two targeted packages in one retail sale. Starting October 1, 2025, manufacturers that sell or bring these products into Illinois must pay monthly fees to the Central Repository, and sellers linked to unpaid fees can face fines.

IL-2025-HB3100.s: Starting in fiscal year 2026, the state would require certain convention and tourism bureaus that get grants from the Local Tourism Fund to match at least 25% of the grant amount. It would also change how some money is shared under the Hotel Operators' Occupation Tax Act and the Illinois Sports Facilities Authority Act. The changes would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB3125.s: Illinois law now says that if a driving school instructor applicant must have a set number of practice driving hours, time spent driving with a temporary license counts toward that total. It affects people seeking a license to teach driving school students. The law takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB3129.s: The bill would add mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine to Illinois' list of Schedule III controlled substances, which are drugs with set legal limits. It would also repeal the Kratom Control Act.

IL-2025-HB3182.s: The bill would set aside $709,500 from the state's General Revenue Fund for the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity. The money would go to the Forest Preserve District of Cook County for the Greencorps Chicago and Forest Preserve Experience programs in the Conservation Corps program. It would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB3216.s: The bill would create a $5,000 state income tax credit for qualified physicians who work in hospitals, health clinics, or on their own and serve underserved areas or rural counties or rural towns. It would take effect right away. The credit would affect eligible doctors who work in those places.

IL-2025-HB3248.s: The law requires many health insurance plans and managed care plans to cover laser hair removal when it is prescribed medical treatment and meets accepted medical standards. It applies to people with conditions such as body dysmorphia, hidradenitis suppurativa, polycystic ovary syndrome, and similar skin conditions. The law took effect on January 1, 2026, and the coverage requirement applies to policies renewed or changed after January 1, 2027.

IL-2025-HB3290.s: The law changes how the state pays claims from the Underground Storage Tank Fund, which helps cover costs tied to approved cleanup plans. The Environmental Protection Agency must decide on payment within 120 days after it gets both a full payment request and the report showing the work is done. For certain tank releases reported before June 8, 2010, owners or operators may get fund money for covered costs after a $10,000 deductible, with some past deductible amounts counted toward that total. It became Public Act 104-0291 and takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB3312.s: The bill would create a process for utilities in Illinois to keep and share customer use data. It would require utilities to save consumption records for at least 2 years, and some billing data for at least 15 years, and to send an account holder’s data to a person or group the account holder chooses. It also sets rules for the Illinois Commerce Commission on how data is shared, how it is entered into a benchmarking tool, and how utilities are protected from later misuse of shared data in most cases.

IL-2025-HB3323.s: The bill would require the Illinois Department of Agriculture to set up a grant program. It would give grants of up to $250,000, if money is set aside, to help qualified farmers cover the cost and labor of giving healthy, free food to pregnant women in need who live in the same county or within 20 miles of the farm. The department would also have to make rules for the program.

IL-2025-HB3345.s: The law extends the Hearing Instrument Consumer Protection Act from January 1, 2026 to January 1, 2028. It also changes rules for people who want a license to work with prescription hearing aids, including a limit of 4 written exam tries in any 12-month period. A trainee license can now be renewed once for 6 more months.

IL-2025-HB337.s: Makes a technical change to the Illinois Controlled Substances Act in the section that gives the law its short name.

IL-2025-HB3438.s: The bill would require the state transportation department to do a life-cycle cost review for certain new road projects that have pavement costs over $500,000. It would also change how a transportation advisory member votes on some home window or door replacement decisions, allowing that member to vote only to break a tie. Crash reports would have to be sent in electronically, and that change would take effect on January 1, 2027; the rest would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-HB3466.s: The bill would change Illinois property tax rules for some residential property that gets a lower assessed value for affordable housing projects. It would let properties keep their eligibility period if a county later opts out, and it would make the program available to qualifying homes even if they also have other public financing or subsidies. It would also require county tax officers to post and accept application forms, and it would have the Illinois Housing Development Authority publish yearly spending rules for the program.

IL-2025-HB3517.s: This bill would give money from the General Revenue Fund to the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity for a grant to the Joliet Area Historical Museum. The grant would help pay for expenses tied to restoring the property that was formerly the Joliet Correctional Center. It would also allow the money to be used for prior year costs.

IL-2025-HB3525.s: The bill would change Illinois rules for gas and building heating, including limits on building heating emissions and a 2050 clean heat standard. It would affect gas utilities, new customers, building owners, and people covered by utility energy-efficiency programs. Some gas utility energy-efficiency rules would start on January 1, 2027, and the Illinois Commerce Commission would review gas line extension charges.

IL-2025-HB3604.s: The bill would remove the state ban on building new nuclear power reactors in Illinois that are larger than 300 megawatts. It would affect power companies that want to build new nuclear plants in the state.

IL-2025-HB3614.s: The bill would bar carbon capture storage, called carbon sequestration, in a storage site that sits over, under, or through a sole-source aquifer, which is a main water source. It would also define what a sole-source aquifer is, and it would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB3628.s: The bill would give money to the Illinois Department of Public Health for grants, costs, and admin work tied to HIV/AIDS programs. It also would fund efforts to prevent, screen for, and treat sexually transmitted infections, and to help people get pre-exposure prophylaxis, or PrEP, which helps prevent HIV. The measure would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB3698.s: The bill would change Illinois election law rules for spending on campaigns. It sets rules for independent spending, election spending, and spending done together with a campaign, and it changes the term "electioneering communication" to "election spending." It would affect people and groups that spend money in elections.

IL-2025-HB3744.s: Changes Illinois rules for shipping irradiated nuclear reactor fuel. Shippers and carriers would have to tell the state emergency agency at least 7 days before transport, instead of 24 hours, and the law adds new word definitions for these terms. It also lets the agency collect, store, and dispose of stray radiation sources that pose a public health, safety, or environmental threat, and it can seek actual costs from the person tied to that material. Became law as Public Act 104-0330, effective January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB3800.s: Changes several Illinois insurance and health coverage rules. It requires certain insurers to set up a department to handle customer questions and complaints, and it makes other updates to health plan and insurance law, including coverage rules for some tests and jaw injury care. It also dissolves a state fund and sends future money for it to the General Revenue Fund.

IL-2025-HB3849.s: The law lets any authorized worker at a hospice or home health group pick up a patient’s prescription orders, including controlled drugs, and bring them to the patient. It applies to people getting hospice care or home health services. It took effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB398.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Freedom from Drone Surveillance Act, in the part that names the law. It affects the wording of that law, not a new program or penalty.

IL-2025-HB444.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Farm Fresh Schools Program Act. It affects the part of the law that names the act. The change is in a section about the short title, which is the law's official name.

IL-2025-HB4443.s: The bill would create a new state fund called the Illinois Future Fund and set up a monthly $500 cash aid program for people who qualify. It would let the Department of Human Services write the rules for the program and change how money from cannabis taxes is split over time, moving more of that money into the new fund starting in 2027.

IL-2025-HB448.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Childhood Hunger Relief Act, in a section about the short title. It would affect that law’s wording, not its main program details.

IL-2025-HB461.s: This bill would make a technical change to the Higher Education Fair Admissions Act. It affects the law’s short title section, which is the part that names the law.

IL-2025-HB4736.s: The bill would change how Illinois taxes estates that include qualified farm property. It would set a $6 million exemption for these estates when figuring the state death tax credit, instead of a $4 million exclusion, and that amount would go up each year with inflation. It would also change how a surviving spouse’s unused tax break is figured, let farm property be valued under a special farm-use rule, and change who counts as a qualified heir. It would take effect January 1, 2027.

IL-2025-HB4773.s: Creates a state fund called the Illinois Climate Change Superfund to collect payments tied to climate change liability from responsible parties. It directs the state environmental agency to set rules for how liability is assigned, how money can be spent, and how the program would work. At least 40% of the money would go to projects that directly help disadvantaged communities facing climate change impacts.

IL-2025-HB479.s: The bill would make a technical change to the School Code section about the law’s short title. It affects the state school law text, not a specific program or benefit.

IL-2025-HB4922.s: The bill would create a grant program run by the Illinois Department of Agriculture for certain farmers. It would give grants to help increase farm output, keep farms strong, and make it easier to sell products. It also sets out who can apply, how grants can be used, how awards are chosen, and reporting rules. The program would start July 1, 2026.

IL-2025-HB497.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Consumer Coverage Disclosure Act, in the part that gives the law its short name. It affects that state law and appears to change wording only.

IL-2025-HB4990.s: The bill would update Illinois rules on preventing sexual violence in higher education. It would require college policies to cover sexual harassment, change how complaints are handled, and adjust the roles of confidential and complaint advisors. It would also let survivors sue in civil court and would take effect July 1, 2027.

IL-2025-HB508.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Customized Employment for Individuals with Disabilities Act, in a section about the short title. It affects that law’s wording, but no other change is described in the summary.

IL-2025-HB511.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Family Bereavement Leave Act, in the section that gives the law its short name.

IL-2025-HB5198.s: The bill would change rules for affordable housing plans in Illinois. It would require some local governments to give residents notice and a chance to speak at a public hearing before they adopt a plan, and to show proof they did that when they send the plan to the state housing agency. It would also ask the plan to name the best land for affordable housing, set timelines for key steps, and include possible incentives to help attract such housing.

IL-2025-HB5282.s: Would make a technical change to the Illinois Municipal Code in the section about the short title.

IL-2025-HB529.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Agricultural Fair Act, in a section about the short title. It affects the wording of the law, not the program itself.

IL-2025-HB540.s: Makes a technical change to the Private Activity Bond Approval Act, in the part that gives the law its short name.

IL-2025-HB5436.s: Starting August 7, 2028, regional superintendents of schools would take over the duties now handled by regional boards of school trustees and would appoint a 5-member nonpartisan citizens committee to do that work. It would extend the terms of current board members until that date and move the boards' records and property to the local education office or service center that serves the same area. It would also remove the old board rules from state law and make related changes in other laws. The bill would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB5513.s: The bill would set new environmental, water, and energy rules for hyperscale data centers in Illinois. It would require public notice, community benefit agreements, water use reports, water planning, and yearly energy and water reports, and it would create fees and funds tied to the centers’ peak power use. It would also require cities and counties to use an online solar permit system for home solar projects by July 1, 2027.

IL-2025-HB554.s: Would make a technical change to the state law on information technology accessibility.

IL-2025-HB5568.s: The bill would add medical examiner and coroner offices to the law’s list of medical facilities. It would also say the law does not shield a public worker, medical facility, or local government from liability for harm caused by negligent or wrongful handling, identification, disposal, or treatment of a dead person. The change would apply to claims that start on or after the law’s effective date.

IL-2025-HB572.s: Amends the State Fair Gaming Act to make a technical change in a section about the short title. It would affect that law’s wording, not the basic rules it sets out.

IL-2025-HB5757.s: The bill would require a court to revoke pretrial release for a person who was already released for a felony or Class A misdemeanor and was on electronic monitoring, if there is probable cause they committed a new felony while on release. The person would stay in custody while the new charges are resolved. It would apply to defendants in this situation.

IL-2025-HB5798.s: Repeals Illinois's Digital Asset Tax Act. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB5822.s: The bill would let the Illinois Department of Human Services use the Clyde L. Choate Mental Health and Developmental Center for temporary stays of defendants who need treatment while waiting for a permanent placement. It would require the department to evaluate the person, tell the sheriff and court if no placement is ready, and move the person once a bed opens up. It also sets regular reviews during the wait and allows civil penalties if the department does not find a permanent placement within 30 days.

IL-2025-HB5823.s: For people in criminal cases who need mental health treatment, this bill would change how long the state can take to place them in a treatment facility. If the Department of Human Services does not make a placement within 20 days, it would have to pay the sheriff for housing and mental health care after that point, and the sheriff would not be responsible for problems after day 20. It would also change the timing for sheriff follow-up and remove some current 60-day placement and update rules.

IL-2025-HB5824.s: The bill would require a state-run developmental center in Illinois to take back a former resident who moved to a community living setting, if the person or a guardian with placement power asks for it and agrees. It applies when the former resident's medical needs cannot be met in that community setting. If the original center cannot take the person back because it is closing or cutting beds, the person could choose another state-run developmental center if a bed is open. The change would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB5827.s: Starting January 1, 2027, state agencies, school districts, and local governments in Illinois would have to accept a fingerprint-based criminal history check from any certified live scan vendor when they require one for a job, license, or grant. The bill would also bar those public bodies from signing or renewing contracts that block them from accepting checks from other certified vendors. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB5828.s: Creates a state tax credit for people planning certain pharmacy or grocery store projects in Illinois, and lets them use it against withholding tax they owe. It would also let some businesses tied to the state’s economic deal program get enterprise zone benefits without a separate high-impact business application. The bill would allow grants for equipment upgrades at grocery stores run by local governments, including help paying for point-of-sale systems that can handle SNAP and WIC payments. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB5829.s: The bill would require a court to give makeup parenting time to a parent if their court-ordered time was denied because of a child abuse or neglect report, and the state investigation later found the report to be unfounded. It would apply when the loss of parenting time came from a refusal, interference, or a court motion or emergency order that stopped or ended the time, unless the investigation instead found an indicated report. The makeup time would have to be awarded within 6 months of the unfounded report, and the court could also hold a party in contempt for wrongly denying parenting time.

IL-2025-HB5830.s: The bill would require the Department of Central Management Services to offer Medicare plans for state employees and their Medicare-primary dependents. These plans would help cover Medicare Parts A and B and include coverage for Part D drugs. The department would start buying these plans on January 1, 2027, for use on January 1, 2028, and the bill would take effect right away.

IL-2025-HB590.s: Would make a technical change to the Freedom of Information Act in the section that gives the law its short name. It affects the way that law is labeled in Illinois law.

IL-2025-HB604.s: Makes a technical change to the State Employee Health Savings Account Law, which covers state worker health savings accounts.

IL-2025-HB629.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Bill of Rights for the Homeless Act. It affects that law’s short title section, which is the name used for the act.

IL-2025-HB665.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Community Energy, Climate, and Jobs Planning Act. It affects the part of the law that gives the short title, which is the official short name of the act.

IL-2025-HB675.s: Makes a technical change to the Community Partnership for Deflection and Substance Use Disorder Treatment Act. The change is in a section about the short title, which is the act’s short name.

IL-2025-HB679.s: Amends the Local Government Travel Expense Control Act to make a technical change to the section that gives the law its short name. It would affect local government travel expense rules.

IL-2025-HB722.s: It would make a technical change to the Murdered Children Funeral and Burial Assistance Act, updating a section that gives the act’s short title and how it is referred to. The change would affect how the law is named and cited in that act.

IL-2025-HB754.s: The bill would make a technical change to the law on electronic monitoring in long-term care facilities. It affects the section that gives the law its short name.

IL-2025-HB758.s: The bill would make a technical change to the ID/DD Community Care Act, in the section that gives the law its short title. It affects that law’s wording, not the broader program itself.

IL-2025-HB772.s: The bill would make a technical change in the Public Utilities Act about the short title of the Telecommunications Article. It affects the law that covers telecommunications in Illinois.

IL-2025-HB81.s: This bill would appropriate $2 from the General Revenue Fund to the Office of the Architect of the Capitol for its FY26 ordinary and contingent expenses. It would take effect on July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB88.s: The bill would appropriate $2 from the General Revenue Fund to Chicago State University. The money would be for the university’s FY26 ordinary and contingent expenses. It would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-HB915.s: Changes a section of the Data Governance and Organization to Support Equity and Racial Justice Act to fix the short title wording.

IL-2025-HB929.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Racial Impact Note Act’s short title section. It affects how that law is named in state law.

IL-2025-HB962.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Illinois Highway Code section that gives the law its short title.

IL-2025-HB993.s: Would make a technical change to the Child Passenger Protection Act, in the part that names the law.

IL-2025-SB1044.s: Changes a part of Illinois county economic development tax rules by making a technical fix to the short title section. It affects the law that deals with county economic development project areas and property tax sharing.

IL-2025-SB1045.s: The bill would make a technical change to the Drug School Act in the section that names the law. It affects that law’s short title, not a program change.

IL-2025-SB1158.s: The law makes a technical update to the Toll Bridge Act, changing a section about the act’s short title. It affects the wording of that law and takes effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB119.s: Changes the rules for syphilis testing during pregnancy in Illinois. It would require the appropriate health care professional caring for a pregnant person to do a test at the first visit and another during the third trimester, between 27 and 32 weeks. It also changes who files birth and stillbirth reports. The law takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB1208.s: The bill would let some out-of-state adults carry a handgun in Illinois if they have a similar permit or a permit from a state with a reciprocal agreement, are U.S. residents, and are not Illinois residents. Those people would have to follow the same rules as Illinois permit holders. If they later move to Illinois, their permit would stay valid here for 90 days, and the measure would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1212.s: The bill would change the state's concealed carry rules for firearms. It would let people carry in rest areas and in buildings at rest areas that are run by the Illinois Department of Transportation. The change would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-SB1232.s: The bill would set aside part of state disaster grant money for small towns with 5,000 people or fewer, so they can get help faster after a disaster. It would let the Illinois Emergency Management Agency send those funds through the local EMS system to cover things like debris removal and other needed disaster services. The town would have to show the services are needed for recovery, and the change would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1256.s: People who get disability license plates or a parking decal or device would have to show proof of their permanent disability every 5 years. The law applies to permanently disabled applicants and takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB1262.s: The bill would require the Illinois Department of Innovation and Technology to set up a system that lets people automatically translate state website content into another language. It would have to work for at least the 100 most commonly spoken languages in the state. The change would take effect right away, and it would apply to websites run by the state.

IL-2025-SB1274.s: The law lets a sexual assault services voucher be used to pay for taxi rides and car-share programs. It also gives a plain definition of what a car-share program is. It became law and takes effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB1308.s: The bill would give $7,200,000 to Western Illinois University to help pay for operations at its Innovation Campus in the Quad Cities. It affects Western Illinois University and the campus program there. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1309.s: The bill would let the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity approve one more pilot River Edge Redevelopment Zone in the city of Sterling. A redevelopment zone is a set area used for planned economic development.

IL-2025-SB1319.s: The bill would require $27,000,000 each month to be moved from the Road Fund to the Department of Transportation. The department would then send the money to cities, counties, and road districts in the state using a set formula.

IL-2025-SB133.s: The bill would exempt certain motor vehicles from several Illinois sales and use taxes if the vehicle is registered in Illinois to a resident who bought it while stationed outside the state on active military duty. It would affect Illinois residents in the military who meet those conditions.

IL-2025-SB1376.s: Creates a law that requires every public and private college or university to post its cost of attendance on its website for the 10 school years before the law takes effect and for each year after that. The posted costs must show which expenses are included in IRS Form 1098-T and which are not. It became law and takes effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB1395.s: The bill would set new rules for prisons to better serve people with intellectual or developmental disabilities. It would let them skip certain basic-skills tests for school, work, and job training programs, and still count that participation toward earned sentence credit. It would also require yearly staff training and allow people denied access or help to use the prison grievance process.

IL-2025-SB1396.s: The bill would change the Property Tax Code rules for expanded county review boards in emergency cases. In Lake, DuPage, McHenry, and Kane counties, it would remove a rule that let nearby county residents be named as extra board members. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1404.s: The bill would require the Illinois Department of Agriculture to run a program to help bring fresh, healthy food and nutrition education to food deserts, which are areas with limited access to healthy food. It would support projects in those areas and help share best practices on food access and food preparation education. The program would affect people and groups working in or serving food deserts, including nonprofit groups and other interested parties.

IL-2025-SB1428.s: The bill would make annual or 3-year fishing licenses, sportsmen’s combination licenses, and hunting licenses free for Illinois resident Gold Star Family members. It would also have the Department of Natural Resources set the rules for who qualifies and what proof is needed. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1449.s: The bill would let a downstate forest preserve district ask voters to approve a special tax on retailers and services. If approved, the money would go only to forest preserve uses such as education, outdoor recreation, upkeep, operations, public safety, trails, and buying or restoring land.

IL-2025-SB1467.s: The law changes several rules in the Illinois Vehicle Code for vehicle titles, registration, and driver records. It says some personal details on title and registration forms, like a photo, signature, Social Security number, email, and medical or disability info, must stay private except for certain people. It also changes antique vehicle registration fees and insurance notice timing, and it took effect on August 1, 2025.

IL-2025-SB1473.s: The bill would change parts of Illinois horse racing law, including rules for organization licenses, race meetings, and wagering. It would also add rules for standardbred racetracks in Cook County and Macon County. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1481.s: The bill would change the timing for park district board elections after voters or the board change the number of board seats. It would also change when an appointed member stays in office to fill a vacancy and when that seat is filled by election. The changes would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-SB1519.s: Changes the school code so school districts must report each year how often students were referred to law enforcement. It also requires the state education board to publish a statewide report each year and asks school and police groups to make rules for sharing reports on both criminal and civil offenses. School staff may not give students a fine, fee, ticket, or citation for a municipal code violation, and they may not send truant students for punishment fines or fees. It became law on August 20, 2025.

IL-2025-SB1520.s: The bill would let state agencies share some cannabis licensee info to help run social equity programs. It would also expand help for certain social equity cannabis applicants and lottery licensees through the Cannabis Business Development Fund, including loans, grants, and other financial aid to help them get the money and space needed to start a business. It would give the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity more power to set up deals that help with lending or investment, and it would allow some loans to be forgiven or awarded by lot if money is short.

IL-2025-SB1523.s: The law says a person who files a fake or changed deed, or one meant to wrongly cloud or transfer land title, can be held liable to the real owner in court. It also requires every county to keep a property fraud alert system and every county recorder to set up a process to review and refer suspect deeds and other recorded papers. It took effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB1529.s: Election offices would have to keep a website and post election results there, including district data for every district they cover, even if they only cover part of it. The State Board of Elections would set a standard way to name election districts, precincts, and polling places, and it would give election offices rules to follow. The new naming rules would apply starting with the 2026 General Primary Election and later elections.

IL-2025-SB1547.s: In cities with fewer than 100,000 people, if voters approve staggering alderperson terms, the next election would set different term lengths for odd- and even-numbered wards. In a city with an odd number of wards, one alderperson from each odd-numbered ward would serve 2 years, and one from each even-numbered ward would serve 4 years. It would affect city wards and alderperson elections.

IL-2025-SB1570.s: The bill would change Illinois kratom rules so any person could not knowingly buy or have kratom, or sell it, buy it for someone else, give out samples, or provide it to anyone. A kratom violation would be a Class B misdemeanor, and selling or giving out kratom would also carry a fine of at least $500. It would affect people who buy, have, or handle kratom products.

IL-2025-SB1587.s: Starting January 1, 2026, the Illinois State Police would send certain homicide information to the Illinois Criminal Justice Information Authority every three months. The Authority would study the data and post it on its public website every three months.

IL-2025-SB1595.s: The bill would change how the Department of Natural Resources handles construction tied to worst-case flood events under the Rivers, Lakes, and Streams Act. It would set deadlines and review steps for levee improvement requests, allow small water level increases for rural and urban projects near navigable waterways, and require a mitigation review only in some cases. It would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-SB1599.s: The bill would require the Illinois Attorney General to accept required reports filed under the charity solicitation and charitable trust laws online. It would affect charities and charitable trusts, and it would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1632.s: The bill would change the Open Meetings Act for certain licensing boards run by the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation. If a meeting is held at one office and other public locations by video link, members in those places would count toward a quorum when public notice and access are provided. It would affect those licensing boards and their meetings in public buildings.

IL-2025-SB1658.s: The bill would require a jail or state prison to give a person an opioid overdose blocker when they are released if they were held on drug charges or were found to have a substance use disorder. It would apply to county jails and state correctional facilities in Illinois.

IL-2025-SB1675.s: This law updates the Illinois Code of Military Justice by fixing the names of certain military offenses in the law. It also makes a matching change to the rule on conduct unbecoming an officer, which means behavior that is not fitting for an officer. It took effect on August 1, 2025.

IL-2025-SB1680.s: The bill would set new greenhouse gas goals for transportation in Illinois and require the state and planning groups to check whether their plans meet those goals. It would also require emissions reviews before adding some road expansion projects, and it would use a "social cost of carbon," a dollar estimate of climate harm, in planning starting June 30, 2026. For projects costing $30 million or more, the state and planning groups would also have to score how they affect climate equity and access, and they would need to give the public early and ongoing chances to take part in transportation planning.

IL-2025-SB1692.s: The bill would create a new state law for retirement plans offered by local governments and school districts. These plans would have to follow state pension rules on things like fiduciary duties, funding, investments, and participant rights, even if the plan is not set up under the Illinois Pension Code. It also defines what counts as a retirement plan.

IL-2025-SB1705.s: The bill would change Illinois law to treat more electronic machines and devices as gambling devices, including some that use credits, coupons, or sweepstakes tied to buying something. It would also say that a person can still be charged with gambling if a game of skill or chance uses one of these covered devices, even if no payment is needed to play. A gambling offense using one of these devices would be a Class 4 felony, and the changes would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1746.s: The bill would set new rules for health plans that cover prescription drugs starting January 1, 2026. It would bar certain required steps for enrollees and require clinician-administered drugs to follow federal drug supply and delivery rules. It would also make several Illinois public and private plan laws match these same rules.

IL-2025-SB1759.s: The bill would give $50 million to the Illinois Department of Transportation to expand Route 6 from Brisbin Road to Ridge Road. It would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-SB1814.s: Creates a public health definition of amniotic fluid embolism, a rare medical emergency linked to pregnancy and childbirth. It directs the state health department to run a public awareness campaign, share guidance with doctors and other health workers, and post information on its website. The law took effect on August 15, 2025.

IL-2025-SB182.s: The bill would ban carbon storage work over any federally designated sole source aquifer, which is a water source people mainly rely on for drinking. It would also stop the Illinois EPA from giving a carbon storage permit if it knows the project is planned over one of those aquifers. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1856.s: The bill would limit the advisory questions registered voters can ask for a township annual meeting to topics tied to the township’s legal duties under state law. It would affect townships and voters who seek to put these questions before local electors at the annual meeting.

IL-2025-SB1857.s: The bill would expand cash aid and food benefits for foreign-born victims of trafficking, torture, or other serious crimes who are preparing certain immigration applications. It would remove limits that now tie that help to available funding, single-adult status, or living in a place that gives most daily meals. The changes would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-SB1909.s: The law lets Kane County’s transportation office use quick-take land taking for one year after it takes effect. That is for work to realign and separate an intersection. It became law on August 1, 2025.

IL-2025-SB1912.s: The bill would change rules for a workforce program for health care providers in shortage areas. It would add optometry students and optometrists, add some medical sites like rural health centers and federally qualified health centers, and update who counts as a primary care doctor to include obstetricians and gynecologists. It would also change how loan repayment and scholarship money is paid back, and it would take effect on January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB1937.s: The bill would change the Illinois pension code for some state employees who can get an alternative retirement annuity. It would let them start getting an estimated payment within 30 days after they leave work or file for benefits, and the pension system would later fix any difference between the estimate and the final amount. It also says the benefit increase from this change would not count as a new benefit increase, and it would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB1947.s: Changes rules for getting and keeping educator licenses in Illinois. It adds community college staff to a state board, changes some course and test rules, and creates new paths for paraprofessionals and some college graduates to become licensed teachers. It became law and takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB1955.s: The bill would change court record rules for eviction cases and use the word "impound" instead of "seal" for certain files. It would let a court order a file impounded if both sides agree. It would also update related words in the rules for criminal record clearing and change some duties from "court" to "circuit court clerk".

IL-2025-SB1964.s: The bill would set rules for fees in rental deals for homes. It would stop landlords and some rental agents from charging many fees to tenants unless the law allows it, and it would require all tenant fees to be listed on the first page of the lease with a short description. It would also limit some lease terms, like certain late fees, renewal fees, move-in changes, contact fees, eviction-related fees, and pet fees, and the new rules would apply to leases signed after the law takes effect.

IL-2025-SB199.s: The bill would require DUI memorial markers and fatal crash memorial markers to be kept up permanently. It affects the roadside memorial markers covered by the act.

IL-2025-SB2001.s: Requires online marketplaces to check that products sold by some high-volume third-party sellers were obtained legally. It also requires those sites to identify certain sellers as certified, and to warn police if they suspect stolen goods are being sold. The Illinois Attorney General may seek civil fines of up to $10,000 for each violation, plus legal costs. It became law and takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB2008.s: The bill would change the Grocery Initiative Act by adding definitions for "independently owned" and "local ownership." It would affect people and businesses covered by that law.

IL-2025-SB2027.s: The bill would change several Illinois sales and use tax laws for motor vehicles. It would make it harder for some out-of-state vehicle sales to qualify for a tax break if the buyer is a limited liability company with an Illinois member, and it would limit a tax break for limousines to ones not covered by the Transportation Network Providers Act. It would also say the motor vehicle privilege tax does not apply when a retailer buys a vehicle to resell, and it would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB2028.s: The bill would create a tax break for equipment and materials used in providing broadband service. It would apply to items put into service on or after January 1, 2026, and affect businesses that provide broadband services. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB204.s: The bill would change the rules for some judgeships in Illinois’ 6th judicial circuit. It would remove language that says certain at-large judgeships must be changed, as they become open, into judgeships for residents elected from Champaign County and Macon County.

IL-2025-SB2053.s: The bill would change how some tourism grants are matched with local money starting in fiscal year 2026. It would also change how money is shared under the Hotel Operators' Occupation Tax Act and the Illinois Sports Facilities Authority Act. The changes would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB2068.s: The bill would let the Department of Agriculture deny, renew, suspend, or take away a cannabis cultivation center license if a county says the center has not paid property tax or a related penalty owed to that county. It would affect cannabis cultivation centers and county tax payments. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB2096.s: Creates a new law on who can own and run a veterinary practice. It would let licensed vets, and also some people or businesses that are not licensed vets, form a practice in a legal business form to own and operate a place that treats animal sickness and injury, with some limits. It also includes rules for what happens when an owner dies, what can happen for rule breaks, and the relationship with clients.

IL-2025-SB211.s: The bill would change Illinois ethics rules for local government workers and officials. It would require a person’s financial disclosure form to list certain close family members who also work, contract, or hold office in the same local government, along with their job title or what services they provide. The rule would affect filers in local government.

IL-2025-SB2144.s: Creates a new state energy policy law focused on a transparent, inclusive, and competitively neutral power buying process. It would tell the state to consider the strengths of different energy developers and use a process that may bring more competition and lower costs for consumers.

IL-2025-SB2172.s: The bill would change where public agencies post basic information about themselves under Illinois open records law. Agencies with a website would post that info online, and agencies without a website would also post it at their offices. It affects public bodies in Illinois.

IL-2025-SB2178.s: The bill would let a retired police officer carry a concealed firearm on the property of the officer’s former government employer if the officer is allowed to carry under federal law and local rules say it is allowed. It would affect retired officers who meet those conditions.

IL-2025-SB2187.s: The bill would change how Illinois buys food for public colleges and other state facilities. It would require agencies and state-owned facilities to make multi-year plans to better match food buying with set food values on fairness, tracking, and clear records. It would also create a task force and change rules for food labels that may say "Illinois-grown," "Illinois-sourced," or "Illinois farm product."

IL-2025-SB2196.s: Creates rules for electric utilities in Illinois to speed up power upgrades and new service. It would require utilities to plan ahead, order needed equipment, and add workers so homes, businesses, and vehicle charging can be connected without long delays. It also would let some customers use an optional flexible connection agreement, and it would address staffing, cost recovery, and safety. It would take effect immediately.

IL-2025-SB2224.s: The bill would change how Illinois picks its presidential electors. Most electors would be chosen by congressional district, and 2 at-large electors would vote for the presidential and vice presidential candidates who got the most votes statewide. It affects how the state awards its Electoral College votes in presidential elections.

IL-2025-SB2230.s: The bill would let a retailer license holder temporarily store alcoholic liquor in the original container at another licensed retail store if set rules are met. The rules cover things like common ownership, where the store is, how the liquor is handled, and keeping records. It would affect licensed retail liquor sellers.

IL-2025-SB2297.s: The bill would change Illinois procurement rules to let a state agency or public college or university ask for certain purchases to be named continuous improvement procurements. That means some buying contracts could be set up for ongoing process changes and better results over time.

IL-2025-SB2303.s: The law raises fines for people or businesses that offer fire sprinkler contractor services without the right license or an exemption. It also raises fines for people who work as fire sprinkler inspectors without being licensed or exempt. Repeat offenses within 24 months can lead to higher fines, and some of that money goes to the Fire Prevention Fund.

IL-2025-SB2309.s: Changes where certain fees go under the Rivers, Lakes, and Streams Act. Penalty fees and permit application fees would go into the Water Resources Fund instead of the State Boating Act Fund. It became law as Public Act 104-0142 and takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB2312.s: The bill would give $50 million from the Capital Projects Fund to the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity. The money would go as a grant to the DuPage Children’s Museum for capital improvements. It would take effect July 1, 2025.

IL-2025-SB2317.s: For Illinois Department of Transportation construction contracts, extra signature approval would be needed only when a contract is $750,000 or more, or grows to that amount in a fiscal year. The department could set a yearly update to that dollar limit to match higher highway construction costs. The change would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB2322.s: The bill would rename the Illinois Emergency Management Agency Act as the IEMA-OHS Act and update it to refer to homeland security and the Office of Homeland Security. It would change some definitions, remove old salary rules, and add new duties for nuclear and radiation safety and homeland security. It would also create a Homeland Security Advisor, optional deputy advisors, a Homeland Security Advisory Council, a Cybersecurity Commission, and a Statewide Interoperability Coordinator.

IL-2025-SB237.s: Creates a state program that would pay community groups to provide housing, job training, mental health help, and restorative justice services for emerging adults as an alternative to prison. Judges could place eligible people in these community settings instead of Department of Corrections facilities, and the groups would be paid monthly at a rate tied to the cost of incarceration. The Department of Human Services would set standards and monitor providers, and the departments would report on outcomes and costs. It would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB2392.s: The bill creates the Illinois Guaranteed Income Fund in the State treasury. Subject to appropriation, the Department of Human Services would give grants to eligible entities to run pilot programs and other projects that provide a guaranteed income to participants. The department would prioritize projects serving Illinois residents who are pregnant individuals, recent new parents, people facing homelessness or moving into housing after homelessness, formerly incarcerated people or their family members, and people in educational or vocational programs. The bill also sets rules for grant distribution, benefits counseling, reviews and evaluations, and public reporting.

IL-2025-SB2409.s: The bill would require the Illinois Department of Public Health to set special design rules and general safety standards for above-ground pools under the Swimming Facility Act. It would affect people and businesses that build, install, or follow rules for these pools in Illinois.

IL-2025-SB2421.s: Creates a state program for psychiatric residential treatment facilities for people under 21 on medical assistance. The program would be family-driven, youth-guided, and trauma-informed, with youth and family involved in care planning, and the state would seek federal approval for Medicaid coverage of needed inpatient psychiatric care in these facilities. It also sets rules for provider approval and oversight, limits any one facility to 40 beds, creates an advisory committee, and requires the state to post counts of emergency safety interventions and serious events online. The law took effect August 1, 2025.

IL-2025-SB243.s: Changes the Open Meetings Act so a public body may let one of its members join a meeting by other means if that member cannot be there in person because of active military duty. A majority can approve this only when a quorum is physically present, and the bill defines key terms like "active military duty" and "service member." It became law and takes effect January 1, 2026.

IL-2025-SB2496.s: The law updates the Illinois Physical Therapy Act and extends its sunset date, which is the date the law is set to expire, from January 1, 2026 to January 1, 2031. It also changes some job titles and rules for physical therapists, including licensing, exams, fees, discipline, and records kept by the agency that oversees the field. Some parts took effect on August 1, 2025, and the sunset-date change took effect right away.

IL-2025-SB251.s: The bill would set training, certification, or work experience rules for surgical technologists hired or contracted by health care facilities on or after January 1, 2027. It also says people may still do surgical technology work if they are acting within their license or registration, or if they are a student or intern under direct supervision.

IL-2025-SB26.s: The bill would require Illinois courts to use Illinois law, including its rules for picking which law applies, when deciding a parent-child relationship. The law used could depend on where the child was born or where the child lives now or has lived before, and it would take effect right away.

IL-2025-SB275.s: The bill would change juvenile court rules for minors age 15 or older who are arrested for aggravated vehicular hijacking. It would require them to be held in a detention facility until a hearing, where a judge would decide if there is enough reason to keep them in secure custody. If that is found, they would stay held until the court finishes the delinquency hearing process.
